question.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x+4y-2z \\ -3x-6y+3z \\ 4x+8y-4z\end{aligned}].$ Find $\,\text{Ker}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $T$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $T.$

Fror the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -3 & -6 & 3 \\ 4 & 8 & -4\end{aligned}].$ 

Setting $x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],$ we then need to solve the equation $Tx=0.$ First, we find reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -3 & -6 & 3 \\ 4 & 8 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables, $y,$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

From the first equation, we get 

$$
x=-2y+z.
$$

  

Therefore, the kernel of the linear transformation $\,T$ is ${[\begin{aligned}-2y+z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\,:\,y,z\in R}.$
